mac_setup_notes: Sources: $HOME/projects/libredb/libredb-studio/docs/llms/methodology.md, setup.md, model-tuning.md, README.md, and the shipped profile file src/lib/agent/model-tuning/measured-profiles.json (all read-only). Hardware: Apple M5 Max, 64 GB unified memory, 2 TB SSD, macOS high-power mode on AC (methodology.md "The machine"). Per apple.com/macbook-pro/specs (fetched 2026-11-16), 64 GB is sold only with the 40-core-GPU M5 Max, which has 614 GB/s memory bandwidth. The 32-core variant has 460 GB/s and comes only with 36 GB. Against this laptop's 896 GB/s that is 1.46x more bandwidth here for a model that sits fully in VRAM (estimate). Runtime: Ollama 0.32.13 and 0.33.0 through the OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint. The engine version changed results for gemma4:12b (5/5 on 0.32.13, 1/5 on 0.33.0), so results are claims about a tag on a named engine. The stated measurement date is 22-23 August 2026, but granite4.2 was released 2026-08-25 and its Ollama tag shows "updated 2 months ago", so at least some lane results come after that date or from a tag rebuilt since. Harness: LibreDB Studio Agent mode, embedded SQLite sample, six surfaces x 5 consecutive passes = 30/30 per model. Per-turn limit: 90 s, the shipped default. All eight lane models were measured at 90 s and none is among the nine models with 150 s. Sampling is forced to temperature 0, top_p 1 for every lane model, overriding the Ollama tag defaults (ministral-3 0.15, magistral 0.7/0.95, granite4.2 1.0/0.95). Think settings: magistral runs with reasoning left on (its plan cell takes 5 s). suppressPlanReasoning and suppressAgentReasoning are false for all lane models, so granite4.2:8b ran with its template default, which is thinking on. Context: no lane page states a context bound. On a 64 GB Mac, Ollama's VRAM rule (>= 48 GiB gives 256k) probably applied, capped at each model's maximum, but this is not recorded. Only qwen3.6 pages mention OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=32768. On this laptop Ollama defaults to 4k (docs.ollama.com/context-length), so the harness and OpenCode both need OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH set. Harness crutches that OpenCode does not provide: granite4.1:8b needs refusalExamples=true and retryEmptyTurn=true (24/30 at defaults). magistral:24b needs reportReminderLimit=2, and the profile JSON also has retryUnreadStop=true, which its doc page does not mention. cogito:32b needs planStatementRetries=1, and that is load-bearing: without it the plan cell is 4/5. Durations are whole agent runs (median and slowest run), not tok/s. The methodology calls them a best case and says the pass/fail column is the transferable part. Sustained-load throttling was re-measured away on a rested machine. Correctness of the SQL is largely unchecked, the harness uses one small database, and a fallback prose tool protocol exists for endpoints without native tool calls (setup.md).

models.fit_detail: Weights 6,022,221,312 B = 5.61 GiB (Ollama blob, Q4_K_M, includes vision). KV 139,264 B/token at f16: 64k = 8.5 GiB f16 (total about 14.8 GiB with buffers, too tight against 15.47 GiB) or 4.25 GiB q8_0 (total about 10.5 GiB). 128k with q8_0 is about 14.8 GiB, tight. models.speed_here_vs_mac: Faster (estimate). Fully in VRAM, decode is bandwidth-bound: the ceiling is about 896/6.0 = 149 tok/s here against 614/6.0 = 102 tok/s on the Mac, about 1.46x. CUDA prefill should also beat Metal. The harness's 13s median is a whole run, so expect a similar or shorter run, not a 1.46x-shorter one.
models.best_runtime_here: Ollama is fine because it fits whole, and it is the runtime the 30/30 evidence comes from: OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=65536, OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1, OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0. For OpenCode at 128k, use llama.cpp with the official GGUF, -c 131072 -fa on --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0, plus GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1.
models.reason: Cheapest reliable tool-caller in the lane: 30/30 at defaults with no harness crutches, a short tail (26s), and a comfortable fit at 64k with q8_0 KV. The KB's weak coding scores still argue against making it the main OpenCode model, but it is a strong candidate for a fast sub-agent or tool-loop model and should be smoke-tested in OpenCode.

kb_implications: Ministral 3 8B and 14B are excluded in docs/model-selection.md line 305 for 'weak or missing agentic scores', but the user's own harness has both at 30/30 at the compiled defaults, every cell on its first attempt (measured on the M5 Max, libredb-studio). Move them from Excluded to Honorable mentions as 'reliable tool-calling sub-agent, fits fully in VRAM'. Keep them out of the top 10 for coding: AA TB 9.7% still stands, and the harness does not test code edits. Add an Ollama alternative line, ministral-3:8b (6.0 GB, Q4_K_M) with OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=65536 and q8_0 KV, to llamacpp/models.md or the honorable-mention row.

Granite 4.2 8B: the exclusion holds. The harness passes it, but at a 46s median and 1:56 slowest run, its Assess cell re-read 4/5, and the libredb page itself recommends granite4.1:8b instead. Add a caveat that the current Ollama granite4.2:8b tag has no template layer and no tools or thinking badge (checked live 2026-11-16), so serve it on llama.cpp or vLLM (qwen3_coder parser) as the KB feasibility record already says, not through Ollama.

Add to Excluded, with the reasons now measured: Magistral Small 2506 (magistral:24b), because max_position_embeddings is 40,960 (HF config, Ollama shows 39K), so it cannot meet the 64k OpenCode floor. Granite 4.1 30B (17.5 GB) and Cogito v1 32B (19.85 GB), because they are dense, exceed 16 GB VRAM before KV, and would run at DDR5 speed. The last two pass the user's harness, so the reason is fit, not quality.

Granite 4.1 8B (2026-04, inside the KB window) is absent from the KB. Record it as evaluated: it is the fastest in the lane on the user's harness but needs harness-side retries (24/30 at the defaults: empty turns and malformed tool objects), which predicts OpenCode failures. At most a trial candidate behind ministral-3:8b.
